class.name: OcgTDFChilditerator
class.brief_description: Iterates on the children of a label, at the first level only. It is possible to ask the iterator to explore all the sub label levels of the given one, with the option "allLevels".
class.description: ! Iterates on the children of a label, at the first ! level only. It is possible to ask the iterator to ! explore all the sub label levels of the given one, ! with the option "allLevels".

method.name: default
method.description: Creates an empty iterator object to explore the children of a label.

method.name: from_2
method.description: Constructs the iterator object defined by the label aLabel. Iterates on the children of the given label. If <allLevels> option is set to true, it explores not only the first, but all the sub label levels.

method.name: Initialize
method.description: Initializes the iteration on the children of the given label. If <allLevels> option is set to true, it explores not only the first, but all the sub label levels. If allLevels is false, only the first level of child labels is explored. In the example below, the label is iterated using Initialize, More and Next and its child labels dumped using TDF_Tool::Entry. Example void DumpChildren(const TDF_Label& aLabel) { TDF_ChildIterator it; TCollection_AsciiString es; for (it.Initialize(aLabel,Standard_True); it.More(); it.Next()){ TDF_Tool::Entry(it.Value(),es); std::cout << as.ToCString() << std::endl; } }

method.name: More
method.description: Returns true if a current label is found in the iteration process.

method.name: Next
method.description: Move the current iteration to the next Item.

method.name: NextBrother
method.description: Moves this iteration to the next brother label. A brother label is one with the same father as an initial label. Use this function when the non-empty constructor or Initialize has allLevels set to true. The result is that the iteration does not explore the children of the current label. This method is interesting only with "allLevels" behavior, because it avoids to explore the current label children.

method.name: Value
method.description: Returns the current label; or, if there is none, a null label.
